title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-07-16
lineage: SBD -> Reel Master (10 Inch Reels @ 15ips 1/2trk) -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Stunning early‑Dead performance captured on a crisp soundboard transfer – Pigpen’s organ shines and early jams like “Standing on the Corner” and “In The Pines” are smoking.
ai_review.review: The July 16 1966 Fillmore show bursts with the raw energy of the band’s formative year, delivering blues‑rock classics and quirky jams that many reviewers call a must‑have. The Charlie Miller soundboard transfer is praised for its clarity and vivid organ presence, though a few note Jerry’s guitar sits slightly low in the mix. Overall the recording offers an excellent listening experience of one of the Dead’s most celebrated early concerts.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 5‑star, highlighting both a high‑energy show and a crisp soundboard transfer; only minor mix balance comments appear, leading to an overall rating near the top of the scale.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller’s SBD transfer is described as crisp and clear with a well‑defined Pigpen organ; vocal track panned left, music right. A few listeners wish Jerry’s guitar was higher in the mix, but no major dropouts or distortion are reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early set delivers blues‑rock and country flavors; second set flows tightly with memorable jams that capture the band’s 1966 experimentation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Strong playing noted, but a few reviewers mention his guitar sits a bit low in the mix; praised for ‘Starfire’ tone.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is highlighted as clear and outstanding, described as the 'sound' of the early Dead.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann referenced via the cover of Bill Monroe’s “In The Pines”; drums support the high‑energy performance.
